issues.detail: The Greek 'ο κυριος αυτου' (his master) is translated as 'chủ' (master), omitting the possessive 'αυτου' (his). While minor, it slightly shifts the specific relationship.

The Greek 'ο ελθων' (the one coming/when he comes) is rendered as 'khi chủ đến' (when master comes). The Vietnamese version omits the subject of 'coming' or fails to clearly link it to the master in a way that preserves the specific Greek construction of the participle.
